Tennessee law sets out when a person occupying land can claim title by adverse possession, and how an owner can remove someone who has no right to be there.

What the official sources say

  • Under the statutory forms, seven years' adverse possession under a recorded assurance of title (color of title) is required; section 28-2-102 gives a defense when there is assurance of title and seven years' possession, covering the entire boundary described. (Tenn. Code Ann. 28-2-101 to 28-2-103, as described in Cumulus Broadcasting v. Shim (Tenn. 2007); source)
  • Section 28-2-103, which does not involve color of title, protects an adverse holder after seven years only as to the portion in actual possession. (Tenn. Code Ann. 28-2-103, per Cumulus Broadcasting v. Shim; source)
  • Common-law adverse possession: uninterrupted, continuous possession for 20 years raises a presumed grant or deed; color or assurance of title is not required. (Cumulus Broadcasting v. Shim (Tenn. 2007); source)
  • Possession must be exclusive, actual, adverse, continuous, open and notorious for the required period. (Cumulus Broadcasting v. Shim; Tenn. Supreme Court press release, 7/31/2024; source)
  • Tax payment: 28-2-110(a) bars any action to recover real estate by a claimant who and whose predecessors failed to have it assessed and pay state and county taxes for more than 20 years. (Tenn. Code Ann. 28-2-110(a), quoted in Cumulus Broadcasting v. Shim; source)
  • Landlord detainer types: forcible entry and detainer (29-18-102), forcible detainer (29-18-103), unlawful detainer (29-18-104). (TN Courts, Landlord Tenant Update presentation; source)

Tennessee Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Tennessee Eviction Notice Rules sale
  • Turn the Tennessee Eviction Notice Rules offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Tennessee House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • URLTA notice periods listed: fourteen-day, seven-day (repeat violations), three-day (violence, threats, unsanitary conditions); waiver of notice for nonpayment is possible. (TN Courts, Landlord Tenant Update presentation; source)
  • Non-URLTA notices listed: 14 day, 30 day, 3 day. (TN Courts, Landlord Tenant Update presentation; source)
  • When judgment is for the plaintiff and a writ of possession is awarded, it is executed and the plaintiff restored to possession immediately. (Tenn. Code Ann. 29-18 (writ of possession), per TN Courts presentation; source)
  • Service: personal service on an adult in possession, or after three attempts on different dates, posting plus mailing at least six days before the hearing. (Tenn. Code Ann. 29-18-115 (shown as 29-18-15 in slide), per TN Courts presentation; source)
  • Continuance maximum 15 days unless parties agree, landlord consents or no court is held; defendant appeal within 10 days (29-18-129); certiorari to circuit court within 30 days. (Tenn. Code Ann. 29-18-118, 29-18-129, per TN Courts presentation; source)

Which eviction notice does a Tennessee landlord have to give?

It depends on the county and the reason. Tennessee Courts judicial academy materials on landlord tenant evictions split the state into counties under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA) and every other county, which falls under Tennessee Code Annotated 66-7-101 and following.

Where the rental sitsNotices listed
URLTA countyFourteen day, seven day for repeat violations, three day for violence, threats or unsanitary conditions
Any other county14 day, 30 day, 3 day

Source: Tennessee Courts judicial academy presentation. The slides also note that a waiver of notice for nonpayment is possible in URLTA counties, so read the lease before drafting the notice.

Which Tennessee counties follow the URLTA?

The same presentation lists nineteen counties: Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Greene, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Putnam, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson. A rental in Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville or Chattanooga lands in a URLTA county. A rental in a county outside that list uses the shorter set of rules in Title 66, Chapter 7.

In non-URLTA counties the presentation says only four statutes actually apply: Section 109 on termination of tenancy, Section 110 on tenants with disabilities, Section 111 on service and support animals, and Section 112 on domestic abuse. Ask the clerk of the general sessions court in your county to confirm which set of rules applies before you serve a notice.

What extra rules apply to rent in a URLTA county?

URLTA gives tenants a five day grace period, and Sundays and legal holidays do not count toward it. The maximum late fee is 10 percent. The act also covers security deposits, abandonment, essential services and the duties of both landlord and tenant.

  • Fourteen day notice, the first period the presentation lists.
  • Seven day notice for repeat violations.
  • Three day notice for violence, threats or unsanitary conditions.

A landlord who plans to sell an occupied rental should count the grace period before announcing a default, and should put the reason for the notice in writing, since the court holds the owner to the reasons stated.

How does a detainer warrant move through general sessions court?

Eviction starts with a detainer warrant filed in general sessions court. The presentation lists three types under Tennessee Code Annotated: forcible entry and detainer (29-18-102), forcible detainer (29-18-103) and unlawful detainer (29-18-104). The written notice matters in court, because the owner must rely on the reasons in the notice, and new misconduct after the notice calls for another notice.

Service rules shape what the judge can award. Personal service supports a money judgment. Service on an adult found in possession, service on a contractually named party, or posting can support possession only. For posting, the officer must attempt personal service on three different dates, record the attempts on the warrant, post a copy on the door and mail it, with the posting at least six days before the hearing.

How long can the hearing be delayed and when can the tenant appeal?

A continuance is capped at 15 days unless the parties agree, the landlord consents or no court is being held. After judgment, a defendant may appeal within ten days under 29-18-129, giving bond, or seek certiorari and supersedeas in circuit court within thirty days. The certiorari route requires a meritorious reason and a bond covering costs, damages and the rent for the premises during the litigation.

  • When judgment goes to the plaintiff and a writ of possession is awarded, it is executed and the plaintiff restored to possession immediately.
  • If the defendant appeals without posting the bond for one year of rent, the landlord does not have to post a bond to obtain possession.
  • When a defendant appeals and does post, the landlord's bond must be double the value of one year's rent.

A landlord also earns interest on the judgment from the date of judgment if the tenant's appeal fails.

What if the tenant cannot be found to serve?

The slides describe an "absent" defendant route. Personal service is dispensed with when the defendant is a nonresident, cannot be found and is believed to have left the state, the summons came back "not to be found in my county," the defendant's name or residence is unknown after diligent inquiry, or a domestic corporation has ceased doing business.

In those cases service by publication under Sections 21-1-203 through 21-1-205 applies, and the plaintiff must also post a copy of the publication notice on the front door or other front portion of the premises at least fifteen days before the date set for the defendant to appear. Keep a written record of each attempt to find the person.

What changes when the tenant is in subsidized housing or a domestic abuse survivor?

Subsidized leases bring in a third party. The presentation names HUD, THDA and Rural Development as sources, describes a three way agreement among landlord, HUD and tenant, and says the lease may not contradict the tenancy addendum. Notice requirements for a subsidized unit can differ from state law, so the owner needs written notice that fits both sets of rules.

Domestic abuse has its own protections in both URLTA and non-URLTA counties. If domestic abuse is the underlying offense for ending a tenancy, only the perpetrator may be evicted, and victims, minor children and innocent occupants may not be. A tenant who is a domestic abuse, sexual assault or stalking victim can ask in writing for release from the lease, with a release date agreed within 30 days and a copy of a valid order of protection or documents of a criminal charge.

What should a landlord check before filing a detainer warrant?

Run through the points below in order. Each comes from the court presentation and affects whether a judge can grant possession.

  • Confirm whether the county follows the URLTA or Title 66, Chapter 7.
  • Match the notice type and number of days to the reason for ending the tenancy.
  • Count the five day grace period for rent in a URLTA county, skipping Sundays and legal holidays.
  • Serve the warrant on an adult found in possession or on a named party to the lease, or document three attempts on different dates before posting.
  • Calendar the 15 day continuance limit, the ten day appeal period and the thirty day certiorari period.

A landlord who is also trying to sell should share this calendar with the buyer's agent so everyone plans around the same dates.

How does an eviction affect selling a Tennessee rental house?

An open detainer case, a recent notice and a tenant who may appeal all affect timing. A buyer who is financing may need vacant possession by closing, while an investor may accept the house with the tenant in place. The presentation says a writ of possession is what restores the plaintiff to possession, and a defendant has ten days to appeal, so a sale contract that depends on vacancy needs a closing date that leaves room for both steps.

Bring the lease, every notice, the detainer warrant and the judgment to your title company or closing attorney. Ask the general sessions clerk in the county for the case status before you accept a closing date.

More questions about Tennessee Eviction Notice Rules

How many days of notice must a Tennessee landlord give?

It depends on the county and the reason. The Tennessee Courts presentation lists fourteen, seven and three day notices in URLTA counties, and 14, 30 and 3 day notices elsewhere. Check the lease and the notice type for your county.

Which Tennessee counties follow the URLTA?

The judicial academy slides list nineteen: Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Greene, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Putnam, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson.

Does the tenant get a grace period?

In URLTA counties, yes. Tenants have five days, and Sundays and legal holidays do not count. The maximum late fee is 10 percent.

How fast can a landlord regain possession after winning?

Immediately once a writ of possession is awarded and executed. The defendant can still appeal within ten days or seek certiorari within thirty days, and the bond rules decide whether the landlord must wait.

Can a landlord evict a domestic abuse victim?

No, when domestic abuse is the underlying offense. Only the perpetrator may be evicted, and the landlord may not evict victims, minor children or innocent occupants.

Tennessee probate law decides who inherits when there is no will, when a small estate can skip full probate, and who can sign a deed for an inherited house.

What the official sources say

  • A Small Estate (Small Estates Act, T.C.A. 30-4-101 to 30-4-105) means personal property not exceeding $50,000; it cannot transfer title to real estate. (Hawkins County Chancery Court, Small Estates Act Affidavit instructions; source)
  • A small estate cannot be opened until 45 days from date of death; affidavit filed with court with death certificate; original will, if any, deposited with clerk. (Hawkins County Chancery Court, Small Estates Act Affidavit instructions; source)
  • Intestate spouse share: if there are surviving issue, either one-third or a child's share (search/guide excerpt); any part of an estate not disposed of by will passes to heirs in the same manner. (Tennessee Probate Guide (TN Courts), general rules of descent; source)
  • If there is no surviving issue or parent, the estate goes to brothers and sisters and their issue by representation. (Tennessee Probate Guide (TN Courts); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

When property tax goes unpaid in Tennessee, the statutes allow the taxing authority to sell a lien or the property itself, and they give the owner a set time to redeem.

What the official sources say

  • Redemption: one year from entry of the order confirming the tax sale to the tax sale purchaser. (T.C.A. 67-5-2701(a)(1)(D), per TN Courts delinquent tax handout; source)
  • Redemption period can be shortened to 30 days if the purchaser shows the property is vacant and abandoned by 3 periodic inspections over two months at different times of day. (T.C.A. 67-5-2701(n), per TN Courts delinquent tax handout; source)
  • A redeeming taxpayer pays delinquent taxes, penalty, interest, court costs and interest on the purchase price at 1% per month, levied from the date of sale and on the first day of each month until 30 days after the motion to redeem is filed. (T.C.A. 67-5-2701(b); Tenn. Attorney General Opinion 15-22; source)
  • Motion for lawful charges must be filed within 30 days after mailing of the notice of redemption. (T.C.A. 67-5-2701(d), per TN Courts delinquent tax handout; source)
